prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens reloaded from TokenStorage never get token_expiry_time restored, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired token as valid, the proactive refresh check is skipped, and the client sends a dead access token until it gets a 401. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Tokens reloaded from TokenStorage never get token_expiry_time restored, so is_token_valid() treats a stale/expired token as valid, the proactive refresh check is skipped, and the client sends a dead access token until it gets a 401. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1784 fixes the root cause with a 4-line change in _initialize() (calls context.update_token_expiry() when stored tokens have expires_in), plus a test fixture for expired stored tokens. #2875's own code comment states the identical root cause ('A provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid') but only works around it reactively by adding a ~15-line refresh-before-reauth branch inside async_auth_flow's 401 handling. Once #1784 restores expiry tracking at load time, proactive refresh correctly detects expiry and the 401 path #2875 patches around is avoided, making #1784 the smaller, lower-risk fix that addresses the cause rather than the symptom.

prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both touch the exact same lines in stdio_server() that construct the write_stream memory-object stream, and both address the same failure mode: because write_stream is created with buffer size 0, a handler task blocks trying to enqueue a message (e.g. a final response) until stdout_writer has fully drained a prior message (e.g. a progress notification), producing head-of-line blocking/stalls on stdio transport writes. prs.title: Fix substring matches in WWW-Authenticate parsing
prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: the WWW-Authenticate header parser was matching auth-param names via naive substring/regex search instead of tokenizing the header, causing false positive matches when a parameter name appeared as a substring of another token or value. Both replace this with a manual, quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer over the header value. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: the WWW-Authenticate header parser was matching auth-param names via naive substring/regex search instead of tokenizing the header, causing false positive matches when a parameter name appeared as a substring of another token or value. Both replace this with a manual, quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer over the header value. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a quote-aware comma tokenizer, but they differ in scope: #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of auth-params, which assumes the header contains a single challenge/scheme. #3041 first splits the entire header into top-level comma segments via `_split_www_authenticate_segments`, then `_extract_bearer_auth_params` scans those segments for a scheme token (partitioning each segment on its first space) and collects only the params belonging to the Bearer challenge, so it can tell a Bearer challenge's params apart from a second challenge/scheme appearing later in the same header (RFC 7235 allows multiple challenges in one WWW-Authenticate value). #3012's approach does not have this scheme-boundary check, so a header with more than one challenge would be parsed as a single flat param list. #3041's diff is also larger (+82 vs +39 lines) reflecting the extra segment/scheme-boundary logic. I was unable to confirm CI status or test coverage for either PR since GitHub API/web access was not available in this session, so this pick is based solely on the visible code differences.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a quote-aware comma tokenizer, but they differ in scope: #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of auth-params, which assumes the header contains a single challenge/scheme. #3041 first splits the entire header into top-level comma segments via `_split_www_authenticate_segments`, then `_extract_bearer_auth_params` scans those segments for a scheme token (partitioning each segment on its first space) and collects only the params belonging to the Bearer challenge, so it can tell a Bearer challenge's params apart from a second challenge/scheme appearing later in the same header (RFC 7235 allows multiple challenges in one WWW-Authenticate value). #3012's approach does not have this scheme-boundary check, so a header with more than one challenge would be parsed as a single flat param list. #3041's diff is also larger (+82 vs +39 lines) reflecting the extra segment/scheme-boundary logic. clusters.pick_reason: Both add a quote-aware comma tokenizer, but they differ in scope: #3012's `_iter_www_auth_params` finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of auth-params, which assumes the header contains a single challenge/scheme. #3041 first splits the entire header into top-level comma segments via `_split_www_authenticate_segments`, then `_extract_bearer_auth_params` scans those segments for a scheme token (partitioning each segment on its first space) and collects only the params belonging to the Bearer challenge, so it can tell a Bearer challenge's params apart from a second challenge/scheme appearing later in the same header (RFC 7235 allows multiple challenges in one WWW-Authenticate value). #3012's approach does not have this scheme-boundary check, so a header with more than one challenge would be parsed as a single flat param list. #3041's diff is also larger (+82 vs +39 lines) reflecting the extra segment/scheme-boundary logic. I was unable to confirm CI status or test coverage for either PR since GitHub API/web access was not available in this session, so this pick is based solely on the visible code differences.
